rulings.restated: Input — All your investment in this business is at risk: you have no nonrecourse loans not secured by your own property, no amounts protected against loss by a guarantee or stop-loss agreement, and no amounts borrowed from someone with an interest in the business (box 32a)
rulings.model: The box 32b test omits part of the IRS condition: amounts borrowed 'from a person who has an interest in the business other than as a creditor or who is related under section 465(b)(3)(C) to a person (other than you) having such an interest'. A related-party loan would pass as at risk, while an ordinary creditor could be read as disqualifying.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding — i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, Some investment is not at risk: "Amounts borrowed for use in the business from a person who has an interest in the business other than as a creditor or who is related under section 465(b)(3)(C) to a person (other than you) having such an interest." The box 32a question names a lender with an interest in the business but omits the related-party prong, so a related-party loan can answer Yes and deduct a loss the at-risk rules would limit. BUG-0290; fix the question with the Schedule C form pass (T-157).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: agent reading for the owner (amb.2025.f7206_plan_attribution, TASKS.md T-041); restatement accepted. The form gives no method for the part of Schedule 1 line 16 attributable to the business; the project prorates by the business's share of net profits, as Form 7206 lines 6 and 7 do for the self-employment tax.

rulings.restated: Add scveh.line9 over every confirmed scveh entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The line is a sum of scveh.line9, but how the vehicle record figures standard mileage or actual expenses is not in the text given. The scope 'within the current person' rather than this business also cannot be checked.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. Line 9 is the sum of each vehicle's line 9 within this business (the sc entry is the parent of its scveh entries, so 'the current person' sum is taken inside this business's entry); each vehicle's standard mileage or actual expense figure has its own transcription, render and class M logs (scveh).

rulings.restated: Input — Did you "materially participate" in the operation of this business during 2025 (for example, you worked in it more than 500 hours, or your work was substantially all the work done in it, or more than 100 hours and at least as much as anyone else; see the seven tests in the instructions for line G), and is the business something other than a rental activity?
rulings.model: The restatement leaves out the oil and gas exception. The IRS text says to check Yes if 'you meet any of the material participation tests ... or the exception for oil and gas applies', and a working interest 'is not a passive activity'. Such a filer would answer No and be refused as passive, which the refusal does not name.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: fixed (BUG-0064). The question now includes the exception for oil and gas (i1040sc p. 4, line G; p. 5, Exception for oil and gas), so a working interest is answered Yes and not refused as passive.
